hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute RUQ abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and fever. Pain may radiate to right shoulder or scapula. Exam reveals RUQ tenderness and positive Murphy's sign (arrest of inspiration with deep palpation of RUQ — pathognomonic). Risk factors: female, forty, fertile, fat (the 4 F's). Most commonly caused by gallstone impaction in the cystic duct. RUQ ultrasound is first-line imaging — shows gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening >4mm, pericholecystic fluid, and sonographic Murphy's sign. HIDA scan if US equivocal. Labs: leukocytosis, mildly elevated LFTs, possible elevated amylase/lipase if concurrent pancreatitis. Treatment: NPO, IV fluids, IV antibiotics (cover enteric gram-negatives + anaerobes — ceftriaxone + metronidazole or pip-tazo), analgesics. Definitive: laparoscopic cholecystectomy (within 24-72 hours).
